newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end mixed in dwindling volume.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end mixed in dwindling volume.

text.p: Israeli shares closed mixed with a positive bias in thin trading as the only active players were option speculators, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 0.18 percent, or 0.34 points, to 188.47 on low turnover of 39 million shekels against 43 million on Wednesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index gained 0.14 percent to 198.88.
"The market is simply boring and the only activity was concentrated in several Maof shares. Less than 50 percent of the Mishtanim shares were traded today," said Danni Scharia at Capital Securities.
"The Maof players (who speculate in Maof options) were using the opportunity to move the market. Even the sharp decline of the shekel was almost unnoticed," Scharia said.
The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2800 shekels against 3.2510 on Wednesday.

"The session opened with mild declines but by midday the market started rising following the shekel's decline. Activity continues to be extremely low and the situation in the market is one of wait-and-see," said a trader at United Mizrahi Bank.

"We predict that the central bank will lower interest rates by less than 0.5 percentage point on Monday and this will have a negative impact on trading. The only good news is that there were no sellers today," he added.
The central bank will announce interest rates for November on October 28. The key short-term rate is now 15.5 percent.

The most active shares were Koor Industries, which rose 1.0 percent to 29,118 on turnover of 2.5 million shekels; Bank Hapoalim, which fell 1.25 percent to 455 on volume of 2.5 million shekels; and Teva Pharmaceutical Industries which gained 0.25 percent to 138,634 on turnover of 2.0 million shekels.
